headline: Giménez returns to Atletico with Deportivo
summary: José María Giménez spent over 10 years at Atletico Madrid, and on Saturday he comes back to the Metropolitano in a Deportivo shirt. Atletico's winning run ended 1-1 in Stuttgart on Tuesday, and they are still 2nd in La Liga on 22 points. Deportivo have drawn 5 of their 9 league games and made 2.13 expected goals at Real Sociedad without winning. Even so, the market makes Atletico 74.3% favourites and gives Deportivo a head start of 1.75 goals; the goals line is 3.0, with over at 49.2%. The win is more likely than not; the size of it is the question.
read: Atletico Madrid are second in La Liga on 22 points and the market rates them about 1.7 goals the better side here, making them 74.3% favourites against a Deportivo team without a win in five. Deportivo have drawn five of nine and create enough xG to trouble the Metropolitano, but Atletico come off a 1-1 in Stuttgart with ten men and only four days' rest.

facts.fact: Atletico's six-game winning run ended with a 1-1 draw at Stuttgart on Tuesday, a game they finished with ten men after a red card.
facts.meaning: They arrive with the run broken rather than their form collapsed, but on a short turnaround.

facts.fact: Atletico are second in La Liga with 22 points from nine games — seven wins, one draw, one defeat, goal difference +11.
facts.meaning: They are the side directly behind leaders Barcelona, and this is the kind of home game a title chase has to convert.

facts.fact: The market makes Atletico 74.3% favourites, with the draw at 16.4% and Deportivo at 9.4%.
facts.meaning: Deportivo's chance is roughly an eighth of Atletico's — a clear mismatch on paper, at the Metropolitano.

facts.fact: Deportivo are winless in five (DLDLD) and have drawn five of their nine league games.
facts.meaning: They are hard to beat but have not turned decent performances into three points.

facts.fact: Deportivo created 2.13 xG away at Real Sociedad this month and still lost 2-3.
facts.meaning: They generate real chances on the road — enough to suggest they can score at the Metropolitano.

facts.fact: The market rates Atletico about 1.7 goals the better side — the handicap fair line is -1.67, trimmed from -1.78 in recent days.
facts.meaning: Atletico need to win by two for the main -1.75 line to pay, which the market sees as almost a coin flip.

facts.fact: The market expects about three goals — the total line is 3.0, with over and under priced almost level.
facts.meaning: A normal-scoring home win is the base case; the market is not pricing a rout.

facts.fact: Atletico have four days between the Champions League trip to Stuttgart and this game; Deportivo have had eight.
facts.meaning: Freshness sits with the visitors, who have not played since 16 October.

sources.fact: Atletico Madrid's six-game winning run ended with a 1-1 Champions League draw at Stuttgart, during which they played with 10 men after a red card.
Julian Alvarez scored his first goal of the season for Atletico in the draw at Stuttgart.
Alex Grimaldo said of Alvarez after the Stuttgart draw: "Julian is our best player. He's been creating chances for a few games now and he needed that goal."
An Atletico defender is reported to miss the Deportivo La Coruna game at the Metropolitano but is expected back a week later at Valencia.
Atletico Madrid sit second in the LaLiga table, behind leaders Barcelona.
Jose Maria Gimenez, now a Deportivo central defender, will face Atletico Madrid, his club of more than a decade, for the first time; he said he asked that no fear clause be included.
Gimenez acknowledged that his time at Atletico Madrid is over.
Deportivo La Coruna go to the Metropolitano looking to spring a surprise at one of LaLiga's most demanding venues, in a match billed as a classic-style occasion.
